findings.description: Every under-lock refusal now already says 'the session is not merged' (fastForward's checkout and CAS refusals, assertTargetAt when fastForward calls it again, assertPullRequestHead). withLedgerKept then adds '; this session is not merged.', so after --accept-debt the operator reads the same sentence twice in one error. Dropping the clause from withLedgerKept would fix it.

The unanchored `|customtransfer` branch (flag `i`) matches any local or worktree key containing the word, not only lfs ones. An operator branch with tracking such as `feature/customtransfer-agent` writes `branch.feature/customtransfer-agent.remote` to local config. pup would then refuse at launch, conductor start and merge, and the message calls it an armed driver from a compromised session. git-lfs needs a `.path`/`.args` suffix to run anything, so requiring that tail, e.g. `customtransfer.*(?:path|args)$`, would still cover the 3.x and main patterns without refusing branch or remote names.

The `customtransfer` catch-all sits after the `$` of the anchored group as a second top-level alternative (`...(?:clean|smudge))$|customtransfer/i`), so a reader has to spot that the last branch is an unanchored substring match; splitting it into its own named constant joined in the predicate would make the two kinds of rule readable.

The `withLedgerKept` rewrite spells the shared clause `kept for the retry, which will not file ...` twice, once in each ternary branch, where only the subject and pronoun differ; a wording change now has to be made in two places.

The new test comment above the four looser-form rows restates the same three facts as the `ARMED_DRIVER_KEY` JSDoc (git-diff.client.ts L311-315), a duplicate WHY under AGENTS.md; drop it or point at `ARMED_DRIVER_KEY`.

Decision 82's "…and runs the program they name; and so are the `lfs.extension.<name>.clean` and `.smudge` commands, which git-lfs runs on every lfs object" still has no referent for "so are"; e.g. "and it also runs the `lfs.extension.<name>.clean` and `.smudge` commands on every lfs object".

Decision 82 says the agent "can be named per remote as `lfs.<url>.standalonetransferagent`", but the key is scoped by endpoint URL, not remote name; "per endpoint URL" avoids a reader expecting `lfs.origin.…`.
Decision 82 was rewrapped wholesale, including paragraphs with no content change (the PR-head and ledger-truth sections, the heading), which buries the real prose edits in the diff.

process_issues.description: The security reviewer reported a safety classifier cut its work short before it finished checking whether session-written conditional includes (`includeIf` gitdir:/onbranch:) can make the config git uses at checkout/rebase differ from what `armedGitDrivers` reads; that pre-existing mechanism is unverified in this round.
